rationale.conceptual: The paper's method combines standard first-principles DFT (PBE-GGA) with a one-dimensional Boltzmann transport equation, requiring understanding of band theory, effective mass extraction, and relaxation time calibration. It is a multi-part documented procedure but not a novel algorithm, typical of a specialized application in thermoelectric materials.
rationale.execution: The reference solve.sh produces the two required CSV files using only a pair of short Python scripts with analytical formulas, bypassing any actual DFT calculations. The hidden checker verifies only monotonicity and relative orderings, not exact numeric values, so no heavy pipeline or multi-tool orchestration is needed to succeed.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires reproducing trends in thermoelectric properties of ZnO nanowires using a combination of first-principles DFT and a 1D Boltzmann transport model. The underlying method is non-trivial but well-documented; the reproduction can be accomplished with simple analytic models because the checker only looks at qualitative trends, making execution easy.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The paper's own DFT calculations on ~100-200 atom ZnO nanowires using PBE-GGA would require moderate CPU memory (~16 GB) and wall time but no GPU; the dataset is a few tiny input files.
